clue.text: It could result in deflation being on the way

definitions.text: It could result in deflation being on the way

blocks.note: surface reading: an economic slump, prices falling on the way to recession
setter's reading: a tyre going flat while you are out on the road

explanation.surface: An economist warns of a coming slide in prices.
explanation.walkthrough: Deflation suggests the economy, but here it is literal air escaping, and 'on the way' means on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A hole in a tyre lets the air out, leaving a flat that halts a car journey.

clue.text: Slight drawl

blocks.note: first meaning: an insult or snub, as a noun
second meaning: indistinct, run-together speech

explanation.walkthrough: Slight reads as an adjective modifying drawl, but it is a noun meaning an insult.
explanation.definitionFit: A disparaging remark is a slur, and blurred speech that runs words together is also slurring.

clue.text: Pay Sarah and Ray differently

indicators.note: done differently means put in another order, so the man's name is rearranged

blocks.note: Sal is a familiar short form of the name Sarah
the name taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: An instruction to remunerate two employees, Sarah and Ray, at different rates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Differently' does double duty: Sarah appears in her pet-name form Sal, and Ray is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Regular wages for a job, especially monthly earnings of a professional, are a salary.

clue.text: Aspired to be a giant in the literary world

definitions.text: a giant in the literary world

indicators.note: the word is told to become something else, so its letters turn into a new word

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An ambitious writer hoped to become one of the great names in literature.
explanation.walkthrough: A literary giant sounds like a great author, but it is Giant Despair, the ogre of Doubting Castle in Bunyan's Pilgrim's Progress.
explanation.definitionFit: In Bunyan's allegory the monstrous keeper of Doubting Castle who imprisons Christian is named Giant Despair.

clue.text: Strong, pure flow in circulation

indicators.note: things in circulation move round and about, so the letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A description of a vigorous, clean current of water moving round a system.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something with great force, might or potency; they are plain synonyms.

clue.text: Recoil from falsehood in sincere confusion

indicators.note: one thing set in another, so the untruth sits inside the other letters
confusion means disorder, so the letters of the adjective are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written before rearranging
a falsehood is an untruth

explanation.surface: Someone honestly flustered shrinks back from being told an untruth.
explanation.walkthrough: Recoil looks like a verb (shrink from), but it is the noun: the springing back of something elastic.
explanation.definitionFit: Resilience is the property of springing back into shape after being compressed, which is exactly what recoil names.

clue.text: Eggs used for a change?

definitions.note: a plural noun for a singular collective: a set of eggs
a descriptive phrase for the car pedal

blocks.note: first meaning: a set of eggs laid and hatched together
second meaning: the pedal pressed when changing gear in a car

explanation.walkthrough: 'A change' sounds like varying your breakfast; it is a gear change in a manual car.
explanation.definitionFit: A brood of eggs laid together is a clutch, and the mechanism disengaging an engine for shifting gears is also one.

clue.text: Straight on, looking neither to left nor right

definitions.text: looking neither to left nor right

blocks.note: first meaning: viewed head-on, as a portrait pose rather than a profile

blocks.clueFragment: looking neither to left nor right
blocks.note: second meaning: facing directly forward

explanation.surface: Directions to a single-minded walker heading forward without glancing aside.
explanation.walkthrough: Both halves describe the same head-on pose, though the surface reads like route directions.
explanation.definitionFit: A portrait or photo taken facing the camera head-on shows neither profile, which is the term for that pose.

clue.text: A singularly unwell American playwright

blocks.note: a, taken singly, is one
unwell means sick

explanation.surface: A dramatist who was, unusually, in poor health.
explanation.walkthrough: Eugene O'Neill wrote Long Day's Journey into Night; the apostrophe is ignored in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Eugene O'Neill, Nobel prizewinning author of The Iceman Cometh, was a leading dramatist from the United States.

clue.text: Tree, one found by the river

indicators.note: something found beside another is placed next to it, so the two parts sit side by side

blocks.note: an ace is the one in a pack of cards
R is the standard abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A single tree discovered growing on a riverbank.
explanation.definitionFit: Acer is the botanical genus name for maples, a familiar group of deciduous trees.

clue.text: Dig to attract interest

blocks.note: first meaning: slang for enjoying or valuing something
second meaning: to grow in value, as savings do

explanation.walkthrough: Dig suggests excavation, and interest suggests curiosity; both are financial or slang senses here.
explanation.definitionFit: To dig something is slang for valuing it, and an asset gaining value over time is said to appreciate.

clue.text: Animated by champagne?

blocks.note: first meaning: lively and full of high spirits
second meaning: an informal name for sparkling wine

explanation.surface: A party guest made lively by a glass of fizz.
explanation.definitionFit: A vivacious person is described as effervescent, and the informal word for sparkling wine is the same.

clue.text: He contributes to the liquid assets of a bank

definitions.text: He contributes to the liquid assets of a bank

blocks.note: surface reading: a depositor adding cash to a financial institution
setter's reading: a volunteer giving real fluid to a hospital store

explanation.surface: A customer paying money into his account.
explanation.walkthrough: Liquid assets usually means cash; here it is literal liquid, and the bank stores donated fluid for transfusions.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who gives a pint for transfusions supplies the stock held in a hospital's transfusion bank.

clue.text: Trying to get away by air

blocks.note: first meaning: fleeing, on the run
second meaning: while airborne, during a plane journey

explanation.surface: A fugitive attempting escape by plane.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone fleeing is on the run, and a passenger airborne aboard an aircraft is also described with the same phrase.

clue.text: Security is brought back into the store

indicators.note: something brought back returns the way it came, so the little verb is read backwards
one thing going into another ends up inside it, so the short piece sits within the warehouse word

blocks.note: a depot is a storehouse
taken as written

explanation.surface: Guards are moved back into the warehouse for protection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Security is' looks like subject and verb; 'is' is in fact the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Money paid up front as a guarantee against damage or default, as with rented property, is a deposit.

clue.text: Suggesting I am practising a trade

blocks.note: contracted to I'm
to ply a trade is to work at it

explanation.surface: Someone proposes that they are carrying on a business.
explanation.definitionFit: To hint at something without stating it outright is to imply it, so suggesting and implying match.

clue.text: Complaint I will put to head

blocks.note: contracted to I'll
a ness is a headland, as in Dungeness on the Kent coast

explanation.surface: Someone vows to take a grievance to the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: Head looks like the boss; it is a promontory, called a ness in many British place names.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint in the medical sense is an ailment or disorder, so a sickness fits.

clue.text: Large town supports a legend of wisdom

indicators.note: in a down entry the supporting part sits underneath, so the settlement comes after the story

blocks.note: a saga is a heroic legend
a city is a large town

explanation.surface: A big town is home to the tale of a wise figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Sagacity is shrewd judgement and good sense, a direct synonym for being wise.

clue.text: He who calls to order audio equipment

blocks.note: first meaning: the chair of the House of Commons, who keeps order in debates
second meaning: a loudspeaker

explanation.surface: Someone who phones to buy hi-fi gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Calls to order' reads as placing an order; it is the Commons chair restoring order.
explanation.definitionFit: The presiding officer of a parliament keeps members in line, and a loudspeaker unit for sound shares the name.

clue.text: Taken in for a fantastic slap-up do

indicators.note: something fantastic is wild and unreal, so the letters of the feast are thrown into a new shape

blocks.note: taken as written, hyphen dropped

explanation.surface: Guests invited to a lavish party.
explanation.walkthrough: A slap-up do is British slang for a lavish party; taken in looks like being invited, but means cheated.
explanation.definitionFit: To be sold a pup is a British idiom for being swindled into buying something worthless.

clue.text: Reveal advice on how to be less reserved?

definitions.text: advice on how to be less reserved

blocks.note: first meaning: to disclose or uncover

blocks.clueFragment: advice on how to be less reserved
blocks.note: second meaning: an urging to speak freely and share feelings

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is the instruction you would give a shy person, read as the phrase itself.
explanation.definitionFit: To expose something is to lay it bare, and telling a guarded person to share their feelings uses the same phrase.

clue.text: Loyal toast drunk in hock, presumably

blocks.note: first meaning: a toast drunk to someone, as to the monarch
second meaning: something pawned, left as security for a loan

explanation.surface: After the loyal toast someone is so drunk they end up in debt.
explanation.walkthrough: Hock is both a German white wine and pawn; the wine pulls toward drinking. The loyal toast is the toast to the monarch at a British formal dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Drinking someone's health is an archaic sense of the word, and an item handed to a pawnbroker is also one.

clue.text: No help as an antiseptic? It could be

indicators.note: the answer is something the words could become, so their letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sceptic questions whether a disinfectant does any good.
explanation.definitionFit: Phenol, also called carbolic acid, was Lister's pioneering disinfectant used to prevent infection in surgery.

clue.text: One way of reminiscing?

blocks.note: surface reading: a method or manner of recalling the past
setter's reading: a literal road, the idiom's path down which nostalgic people stroll

explanation.walkthrough: Way looks like 'method'; it is a road, as in the idiom about a trip into the past.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking a trip down this imagined lane is the idiom for indulging in nostalgic recollection of old times.

clue.text: Take another course in sewing

definitions.note: a phrase pointing to a sewing term

blocks.note: first meaning: to change direction when sailing into the wind
second meaning: a long loose temporary stitch

explanation.surface: A student switches to a needlework class.
explanation.walkthrough: Course suggests a class; it is a sailing direction.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailing boat zigzags upwind by changing heading, and a loose basting stitch is also called by the word.

clue.text: Occasion for the landlord to call

blocks.note: first meaning: an instance
second meaning: the call of a British pub landlord at closing

explanation.walkthrough: A British pub landlord shouts this word at closing to tell drinkers to finish up.
explanation.definitionFit: An instance or occasion is a time, and the closing-hour cry in British pubs is the same word.

clue.text: Pay off vessel going to old navy

blocks.note: a submarine, a naval vessel
O is the abbreviation for old
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A sailor is discharged from a ship and returns to the old naval service.
explanation.definitionFit: To suborn is to bribe or induce someone into wrongdoing, such as perjury, which is a corrupt payment.

clue.text: Outrage otherwise concealed by ill-will

indicators.note: something concealed by another is hidden within it, so the small word goes inside the hostile one

blocks.note: enmity is hostility
or, as in 'do it or else', means otherwise

explanation.surface: Fury disguised beneath a show of hostility.
explanation.definitionFit: An enormity is a monstrous wrong or atrocity, so a shocking crime is an outrage in that sense.
